summary: Koun Kajiyoshi (1904–1984) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Taisho University.
Koyo Sakaino (1871–1933) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He founded Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held posts at Toyo University (circa 1901–1933) and Komazawa University.
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. In 1995, Shimizu was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Department of Cultural Affairs, Nishogakusha University, and Toyo University (assistant professor in 1972, professor emeritus 1977–2000).

Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Senmyō. He served as abbot at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sannei-ji (1882), and taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin.

Kozui Otani (1876–1948) worked in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Gakushuin and Kyoritsu Gakusha under Eun Maeda, he served as the 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914).

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was an Indologist educated at Sanskrit College and Presidency University. He held academic posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

Krishna Kanta Handique (1898–1982) was an Indologist who studied at Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as principal of Jorhat College (1930–1948) and vice-chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Educated at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College under Alexander Duff, he held posts at Hare School and Bishop's College.

Krishna Venkateswara Sarma (1919–2005) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri, holding posts at Panjab University, Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, and the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

Krishnanath Chatterjee is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under teachers including Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.
Kristen De Joseph is an Indology scholar who studied under Arlo Griffiths and pursues doctoral studies at Leiden University under supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies attested in 2018 as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean at Gettysburg College.
Kristin Scheible is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Colby College, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University. She held posts at Harvard, Brown University, and Bard College.

Kristina Myrvold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied and held an editorial post at Lund University, and later served as assistant professor of religious studies at Linnaeus University.

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a sinologist and religious studies scholar educated in Paris. He held major posts at EFEO (circa 1962–1973), EPHE (1972–2002), and the Institut des hautes études chinoises.
Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her MA and served as a research fellow at Eötvös Loránd University.
Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Calcutta under the supervision of Nalinaksha Dutt.

Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ganganatha Jha. He held posts at the University of Allahabad (1924–1956) and was director of the Research Institute at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He worked in the Chamba State Department of Education and at Visva-Bharati University, serving as Adhyaksha (1953–1954).
